artist_statement.text:
"Checkpoint"

Year: 2026

Location: Withheld-


In a country that decides what a woman's body wears, where it goes, and how it is seen — the body itself becomes a checkpoint. Borders are not always walls and barbed wire — sometimes they are fabric, sometimes law, sometimes a gaze.

This image comes from the moment I realized my body has never belonged only to me. There has always been someone deciding on its behalf. What you see in this photograph is not an exhibition — it is the moment the border retreats, and what has always been, is finally seen.


Technical Note:

(Fujifilm X-T4, 16 mm 

F2.8, 1/200 Sec, ISO 320)

4160×6240

300 dpi


Captured with a digital camera. Post-processed in Adobe Lightroom for exposure and color grading, and Adobe Photoshop for background retouching using the clone stamp tool. No composite or generative elements.
